slots.practicalActivity: In your Trailhead Playground, open Setup and tour the Administration section of the left-hand Setup menu (Users, Profiles, Permission Sets, Permission Set Groups, Public Groups, Queues, Roles), writing down what you predict each one controls before the next lessons confirm it.
slots.deliverable: A written list of the 7 Administration-section Setup items with your prediction of what each controls.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Setup > Users and review the existing user list, including your own record, noting the License, Profile, Role, and Active columns.
slots.deliverable: A written summary of your own user record's License, Profile, Role, and Active status as shown on the Users list.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new fictional user (for example Jordan Ellis) with a Salesforce license and the standard User profile, then create and deactivate a second fictional user, confirming the Active checkbox behavior.
slots.deliverable: One new active user record and one deactivated user record, both visible in Setup > Users.

slots.practicalActivity: On the User edit page, open the User License picklist and record every license type available in your org, then note which license each of your Chapter 1 users is assigned.
slots.deliverable: A written list of license types available in your org and the license assigned to each user you created.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Setup > Profiles, confirm you cannot edit a standard profile directly, then clone the Standard User profile into a new profile named BDR Custom and assign it to your new user.
slots.deliverable: One cloned, editable custom profile (BDR Custom) assigned to the user you created earlier.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Permission Set called Outbound Dialer Access that grants one object permission not already in the BDR Custom profile, and assign it to your test user.
slots.deliverable: One Permission Set assigned to a user, demonstrating a permission the user's profile alone did not grant.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a second Permission Set, then bundle it with Outbound Dialer Access into a Permission Set Group, and assign the group to your test user instead of the individual permission sets.
slots.deliverable: One Permission Set Group containing 2 Permission Sets, assigned to your test user.

lessons.title: Login Access, Login Hours and IP Restrictions

slots.practicalActivity: On the BDR Custom profile, set Login Hours to a realistic business-hours window (for example Monday-Friday 8am-6pm) and add one Login IP Range.
slots.deliverable: A BDR Custom profile with Login Hours and at least one Login IP Range configured, documented in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup > Password Policies, review and record your org's current password complexity and expiration settings, then review Session Settings for the session timeout value.
slots.deliverable: A written summary of your org's current password policy settings and session timeout value.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Delegated Administration group, add your own user as a delegate, and grant it the ability to manage users within the BDR Custom profile only.
slots.deliverable: One configured Delegated Administration group scoped to the BDR Custom profile.

slots.practicalActivity: Without instructions, clone a second standard profile into a new custom profile for a different fictional role (for example Support Agent Custom), build one Permission Set and one Permission Set Group for it, and assign all three to a third new user you create.
slots.deliverable: A second complete profile, permission set, and permission set group chain, independently built and assigned to a new user.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick 2 users in your org (including ones you created) and write a full access audit for each: profile, every permission set and permission set group assigned, login hours, and IP restrictions in effect.
slots.deliverable: A written access audit document covering 2 users' complete permission stack.

slots.practicalActivity: Simulate onboarding 2 new fictional users for a role you invent (not BDR or Support), building the profile, permission sets, login/session restrictions, and delegated administration scope from scratch with no lesson-by-lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: A complete, original user-access setup (profile, permission sets, restrictions) for 2 new users in a role you invented.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Setup > Company Information and record every setting shown: org edition, locale, default time zone, currency, and storage usage.
slots.deliverable: A written snapshot of your org's Company Information settings.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new Business Hours entry matching the login-hours window from Chapter 1, then add one Holiday to the org's Holiday list.
slots.deliverable: One custom Business Hours entry and one Holiday entry configured in Setup.

slots.practicalActivity: Review Setup > Fiscal Year settings (standard vs. custom) and the currency setting in Company Information. If multiple currencies are enabled in your edition, enable one additional currency and note the exchange rate shown.
slots.deliverable: A written note on your org's fiscal year configuration and currency setting.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup > App Manager, open the Sales app to see its navigation items, then clone it into a new custom app named BDR Console with a trimmed-down set of tabs relevant to outbound sales.
slots.deliverable: One new custom Lightning app (BDR Console) with its own tab set, visible in the App Launcher.

slots.practicalActivity: In BDR Console, add a custom object tab, reorder the app's tabs, and confirm the change reflects in the navigation bar.
slots.deliverable: A BDR Console app with a reordered tab set including at least one custom object tab.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure BDR Console as a Console app and add a Utility Bar with at least 2 utility items (for example Notes and History) pinned to it.
slots.deliverable: A console-style app with a Utility Bar containing at least 2 configured utility items.

slots.practicalActivity: In Lightning App Builder, create a new custom Lightning record page for the Account object, add or rearrange at least 2 components (for example Highlights Panel and a Related List), and activate it as the org default for that object.
slots.deliverable: One activated custom Lightning record page for Account with at least 2 arranged components.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently build a second custom app (Support Console) from scratch with its own tabs, a Utility Bar, and one custom Lightning record page assigned to a different object, without reusing BDR Console's configuration as a template.
slots.deliverable: A second original custom app with its own tabs, Utility Bar, and a dedicated Lightning record page.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short new-admin orientation document covering your org's Company Information, Business Hours, Fiscal Year/Currency, and both custom apps you built, as if training the next admin who inherits this org.
slots.deliverable: A written orientation document summarizing org-level configuration and both custom apps.

slots.practicalActivity: On an object with records, build a second Page Layout with a different 2-column field arrangement than the default, then assign it to a specific profile via Page Layout Assignment so only that profile sees it.
slots.deliverable: 2 Page Layouts on one object, one assigned specifically to a chosen profile via Page Layout Assignment.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a custom Compact Layout for the same object showing 4 key fields, set it as the primary compact layout, and confirm it appears in the record's Highlights Panel.
slots.deliverable: One custom Compact Layout set as primary, visible on the record's Highlights Panel.

slots.practicalActivity: On the Case object, create 2 Record Types with different assigned Page Layouts and different Business Processes for Case Status.
slots.deliverable: 2 Record Types on Case, each mapped to a distinct Page Layout and Business Process.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a dependent picklist pair (for example a controlling Region field with a dependent City field), configure the value mapping, and test that changing the controlling field filters the dependent field's options.
slots.deliverable: One working controlling/dependent picklist pair with value mapping configured and tested.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Global Value Set (for example Priority Levels with Low/Medium/High/Critical) and use it as the source for picklist fields on 2 different objects, confirming both fields share the same value list.
slots.deliverable: One Global Value Set used by picklist fields on 2 different objects.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable Field History Tracking on one object for 2-3 fields (for example Lead Status), make a few edits to a record's tracked fields, and review the resulting History related list.
slots.deliverable: A record showing at least 3 tracked field-history entries after edits to tracked fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a custom List View with at least 2 filter criteria and 4 visible columns, then edit the object's Search Layout to change which columns appear in search results and lookup dialogs.
slots.deliverable: One custom List View with filters and columns, plus a modified Search Layout for the same object.

lessons.title: Related Lists and Related List Filters

slots.practicalActivity: On a parent object's Page Layout, add a Related List Filter restricting a child related list to show only records matching a condition, such as open Opportunities only, and confirm closed records drop out.
slots.deliverable: One Related List with a filter configured, verified by comparing the filtered vs. unfiltered record count.

slots.practicalActivity: On a second object you have not touched this chapter, independently build a complete layout stack: 2 Page Layouts, a Compact Layout, a dependent picklist pair, and one filtered related list, choosing the business scenario yourself.
slots.deliverable: A second object with a full, independently built layout stack (2 Page Layouts, Compact Layout, dependent picklists, filtered related list).

slots.practicalActivity: Revisit every object you have customized so far and do a full UI polish pass: confirm every Page Layout Assignment is intentional, every picklist that should be dependent or a Global Value Set is set up that way, and Field History Tracking is only on fields that genuinely need an audit trail.
slots.deliverable: A written polish-pass checklist confirming layout assignments, picklist setup, and field history tracking were reviewed across your org's custom objects.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Letterhead with a fictional company's colors, then build an Email Template named New BDR Outreach on that Letterhead, including at least one merge field.
slots.deliverable: One Letterhead and one Email Template built on it, containing at least one merge field.

slots.practicalActivity: Review Setup's Email-to-Case configuration and document the routing address and the record a resulting Case would be created under, without necessarily sending a live test email.
slots.deliverable: A written summary of how Email-to-Case is configured, or would be configured, to route an inbound email into a new Case.

slots.practicalActivity: Confirm Chatter is enabled, post a Chatter update on one of your test records, @mention your own user, and follow that record so future updates appear in your feed.
slots.deliverable: One Chatter post on a record with an @mention, and that record added to your Chatter Following list.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup's Activity Settings, review and enable Allow Users to Relate Multiple Contacts to Tasks and Events, then create one Task that relates to 2 Contacts at once to confirm the setting's effect.
slots.deliverable: One Task related to 2 Contacts simultaneously, confirming the Activity Setting you changed.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the notification channels available in your org (email, in-app, mobile) and customize one notification type, such as a Chatter mention or approval request notification.
slots.deliverable: A written note on which notification channels are available in your org, plus one customized notification setting.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a complete day-one communication package for a new fictional team: one branded Email Template, Chatter following set up on their key records, and one activity-management or notification setting tuned specifically for them.
slots.deliverable: A written package summary listing the Email Template, Chatter setup, and notification/activity setting configured for the fictional team.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup > Sandboxes, review the sandbox types available in your org's edition (Developer, Developer Pro, Partial/Full Copy) and, if a free sandbox is available, create one and note how long creation takes.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison of the sandbox types available in your org, plus one active sandbox if created.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an Outbound Change Set containing one of your custom objects' metadata (its fields and a Page Layout) and walk through the steps to upload it, without necessarily deploying to production.
slots.deliverable: One Outbound Change Set created and populated with at least 2 components, documented with a written step list.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup > Release Updates, review the list of pending or scheduled updates for your org, pick 2, and write a one-paragraph impact assessment for each.
slots.deliverable: A written impact assessment for 2 real Release Updates currently listed in your org.

lessons.title: Monitoring: Setup Audit Trail and Login History

slots.practicalActivity: Make 2-3 deliberate configuration changes (such as editing a profile and creating a field), then confirm both appear correctly in Setup Audit Trail, and check your own recent logins in Login History.
slots.deliverable: A Setup Audit Trail showing your own recent deliberate changes, and a Login History view of your recent logins.

lessons.title: Administration Best Practices and Change Management

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page change management checklist for your own org (sandbox-first testing, change sets, checking release updates, auditing after rollout) and run one of your own earlier changes back through it retroactively.
slots.deliverable: A written change-management checklist, plus a retroactive audit of one earlier change against that checklist.

lessons.title: Administrator Case Study: Onboarding a Sales Team

slots.practicalActivity: Re-create the Meridian Fixtures case study's 5-step sequence against your own BDR Custom profile and user from Chapter 1: confirm users/profile/permission sets, app/business hours fit, record type/layout/field history tuning, email template/Chatter, and a sandbox-first change set with an audit-trail check.
slots.deliverable: A written walkthrough confirming each of the 5 case-study steps was performed against your own BDR Custom setup, naming the specific settings touched at each step.

slots.practicalActivity: Invent a new fictional company and hiring scenario different from Meridian Fixtures (for example onboarding a 3-person support team at a software company), and write a full 5-step onboarding plan mirroring the case study's structure: users/access, org configuration, objects/layouts, communication, and testing/rollout.
slots.deliverable: A written original 5-step onboarding plan for a fictional team, structured like the course's case study.

slots.practicalActivity: Execute your onboarding plan end to end in your Trailhead Playground: create the users, profile/permission sets, business hours/app fit, record type/layout tuning, email template/Chatter setup, and a sandbox/change-set-and-audit-trail check, building every piece yourself with no lesson-by-lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: A fully built onboarding setup in your org (users, profile, permission sets, layouts, communication tools) matching your plan, with a final Setup Audit Trail check confirming the changes.

slots.practicalActivity: Review everything built across all 5 chapters of this course as a single org: confirm every user has the correct profile/permission set stack, every object has sensible layouts and record types, communication tools are set up for at least one team, and you can explain the order of operations you would follow to onboard one more new hire tomorrow.
slots.deliverable: A final written summary of your org's complete administrative setup across users, configuration, objects, communication, and process, serving as a portfolio artifact of the whole course.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can administer a live Salesforce org end to end: creating and securing users through profiles, permission sets and permission set groups, configuring the org's apps, layouts, record types and communication tools, and following a sandbox-first change-management process to safely onboard a new team.
